domain: On-screen visual aids (scan 3D preview, SFP module images)

entries.question: During a scan there's a small spinning 3D rack above "Analyzing rack…" — what is it telling me?
entries.answer: It is a progress animation, not a picture of your rack. The glowing band and the lit shelf travel top-to-bottom as the percentage climbs, in step with the line of text under it ("Preprocessing image…", "Detecting rack boundaries…", "Identifying components…", "Mapping ports and cables…", "Locating incident target…"). Read the step text and the % — the 3D rack adds nothing else, and it ignores taps.
symptoms: Small rotating rack shown above the words "Analyzing rack…"
Wondering whether the animation reflects the rack being scanned
Tapping the 3D rack does nothing
entries.rootCause: MiniRack3D is a decorative WebGL animation driven only by the `progress` number; the scan beam and the lit unit are derived from progress, and the container sets pointerEvents: 'none'.

evidence.snippet:
...

Analyzing rack…

{step}

... {progress}%
const STEPS = ['Preprocessing image…','Detecting rack boundaries…','Identifying components…','Mapping ports and cables…','Locating incident target…'];

// Top → bottom: progress 0% → top unit; progress 100% → bottom unit.
const scanIdx = Math.min(Math.floor((progress / 100) * 5), 4);

entries.question: The spinning rack shown while scanning doesn't look like the rack I photographed.
entries.answer: Expected. It is a fixed model, always the same five shelves (switch, patch panel, server, patch panel, switch), and it is drawn before your photo has been analysed — it can never match your rack. Your real rack appears in the results after the scan finishes, including the Topology tab's 2D / 3D view. Nothing is wrong.
symptoms: Animated rack shows devices that aren't in the photographed rack
Always the same number of shelves regardless of the rack scanned
Technician worried the scan detected the wrong equipment
entries.rootCause: The Scene in MiniRack3D hard-codes five units at fixed heights; it receives only the progress number, never any scan output.

entries.question: The scan overlay shows "Analyzing rack…", the bar and the percentage, but the 3D rack area is empty.
entries.answer:
1. Let the scan finish — the 3D rack is decoration; the step text and % are the real status.
2. If it is blank on every scan on this phone, that device can't start the 3D layer. There is no substitute drawing, so the slot simply stays empty.
Your scan and its results are unaffected. Report the phone model if you want it chased.
symptoms: Blank or black square where the spinning rack should be
Progress bar and percentage still update normally
Only happens on certain phones or tablets
entries.rootCause: MiniRack3D renders a WebGL <Canvas> with a transparent background and <Suspense fallback={null}> — if the 3D context or scene fails to start, nothing at all is drawn while the rest of the overlay (bar, step, percent) keeps working.

  dpr={[1, 2]}
  gl={{ antialias: true, alpha: true, powerPreference: 'high-performance' }}
>
...
  <Suspense fallback={null}>

entries.question: Where does the product photo on an SFP Advisor card come from — is it the exact part I'd receive?
entries.answer: It is a photo of that SKU taken from the vendor or retailer listing the recommendation came from, then cached and served by RackTrack. It appears large on the ★ TOP PICK card and as a small thumbnail on the alternatives and cable rows. Use it as a shape/connector sanity check only — confirm the part by the part number and the buy link before ordering.
symptoms: Unsure whether the picture is a real photo of the recommended module
Photo shows a slightly different label or revision than expected
Wanting to confirm a module before buying
entries.rootCause: SfpModuleImage renders module.imageUrl, which the SFP recommender populates from the product page (or an image-search fallback) and re-hosts from the server's own image cache.

entries.question: An SFP module card has an empty box where the picture should be.
entries.answer: No usable photo for that module, so the image slot is simply left blank — RackTrack never draws a stand-in graphic. The recommendation is still valid: go by the part number, the spec chips (speed, type, distance) and the buy link. If it only happens on a restricted site network, reopen the SFP Advisor tab on a better connection.
symptoms: Blank or white square in place of the module photo
Some rows have thumbnails and others don't
No broken-image icon, just empty space
entries.rootCause: SfpModuleImage returns null when module.imageUrl is missing, and flips to the same null render if the image errors while loading (404 / CORS / decode); there is no placeholder artwork.

entries.question: The photo on the ★ TOP PICK card looks cropped or zoomed in, but the small thumbnails don't.
entries.answer: By design. The large card fills its square slot with the photo, so edges can be trimmed; the small thumbnails fit the whole image inside their box instead. It says nothing about the part. Open the card's buy link to see the vendor's full product shot.
symptoms: Edges of the module photo cut off on the large recommendation card
Same module looks complete in the small alternatives thumbnail
entries.rootCause: SfpModuleImage uses objectFit 'cover' for size="hero" and 'contain' for size="compact", inside fixed-size slots defined in the stylesheet.

entries.question: INTERNAL: why does the SFP Advisor return fewer modules than the source catalog lists?
entries.answer: Internal. The recommender drops every module whose image cannot be downloaded and cached server-side, on the rule that a part the user can't see is not worth recommending. Scraped image URLs are only tried when the host passes a trust gate (page's own domain or a known retailer/CDN); otherwise an image-search fallback runs. If outbound image fetching is blocked, recommendation lists come back short or empty.
symptoms: Advisor shows only one or two options for a switch with many compatible SKUs
Empty SFP recommendation list in an environment without outbound internet
A known-good SKU never appears as an alternative
entries.rootCause: pipeline/sfp_recommend.py filters modules to those with a successfully cached imageUrl after image enrichment, and routes untrusted scraped URLs through an image-search fallback.

evidence.snippet:
